_what: The demo scene is FFmpeg geometry, not a HyperFrames part. Style says minutes of footage round-tripped through a headless render costs ~3% luma per frame, so screen + face inset + punch-ins are all composited in FFmpeg. HyperFrames parts from cutsheet.json composite OVER the result.

span._note: cut 2:31.07 to 11:52.00, the whole demo section

inset.occludes: nothing. Measured across three sampled frames: the agent UI keeps its content in a centre column (x655-1265 sidebar closed, x770-1380 open). The bottom-right inset lands on empty canvas. Only contact is ~12px of the composer's right padding when the sidebar is open.

sourceCrop._why: was 1480@1340,300 which cut the shoulder and sometimes the chin while wasting headroom. Chosen from a four-way A/B on real frames.

reposition._why: bottom-right while he reads CONVENTIONS.md in the LEFT pane (3:36-3:56), then left from 3:58 once 'my staging.yaml' at 3:56.31 makes the RIGHT pane the subject. Moving at 3:38 put the inset over the pane he was actually reading.

punchIns._why: The agent UI renders its content in about 27% of the frame width and the code measures ~13px in canvas terms: legible at 4K, unreadable at 1080p where most of YouTube watches.
punchIns._how: FFmpeg zoompan with a smoothstep ease. Centres are MEASURED and each crop is RENDERED AND READ before use. An earlier version checked only that the crop was stable frame to frame, which a blank region passes perfectly: one punch-in scored 0.0 drift while sitting on empty page. Verify the crop CONTAINS the target, not merely that it does not move.
